summary: Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He held positions there as a full-time lecturer, attested in 1992, and later as Professor of Buddhist Studies, attested in 2013.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), and taught at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg, attested in 2005, under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.

Akio Donohashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976) and served on the faculty at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991 and as professor from ~1992 to 2012.

Akio Tanabe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo (~1984–1988, ~1991–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (2015).

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) was a sinologist and historian of Central Asia. Educated at Kyoto University (~1930–1934), he served there from 1937, becoming professor in 1968, and held visiting professorships at the University of Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto, serving there from 1946 to 1975, and later taught at Waseda University (1975–1985).

Akira Miyaji is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his B.A., M.A., and D.Litt at Nagoya University, where he taught (~1976–2007), and later served as professor at Ryukoku University (2013).

Akira Mukai is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral course at Hokkaido University (~1970–1975). He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978) and professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from Kyoto University, studied at Heidelberg University, and held professorships at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.

Akira Sadakata is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and also studied at the University of Paris. He was a professor and emeritus professor at Tokai University (~1970–2007).

Akira Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University (PhD 1984), later holding professorships at Mie University (~1993–2002), the University of Tokyo (2000–2016), and ICPBS (~2016).

Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and completed doctoral work under Daud Ali, later teaching at the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1957–1962), where he spent his career as assistant, associate professor, professor (~1978–2005), and president (1991–1994).

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He served on the faculty at the University of Tokyo from 1961 and as professor from 1965 to 1991.

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He studied under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, taught at the Australian National University (1965–1973), and directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1976–1996).
Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held academic positions at Taisho University, where he is attested as a professor in 1982 and as professor emeritus in 2014.

Akshay Ramanlal Desai (1915–1994) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Mumbai between ~1938 and 1946, working under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye from ~1942 to 1946.

Alan Fox is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies who earned his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988). He joined the University of Delaware faculty in 1992, serving as an associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under supervisor Parimal G. Patil, also studying under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
